samples.summary: rawAnchor is a public mutable field with an implicit 'must be re-assigned after every setRange' contract instead of an argument to setRange
samples.evidence: selection.ts:703 exposes `rawAnchor` publicly and setRange clears it (712), so every pointer path has to remember to write it back afterwards — text-editor.ts:2038, 2073 and setSnappedRange (2372) each do so manually. A `setRange(range, rawAnchor?)` signature (or a dedicated setPointerRange) would make the invariant unforgeable; as written, any future pointer path that calls setRange and forgets the follow-up assignment silently loses the idempotent-snap property with no type-level signal.

verdict.reason: Verified directly: insertLink's selection branch in packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:3582-3611 does only snapshot + setCursorForHistory + applyInlineStyle(range, {href:url}) (or applyStyleToCellRange) — no linkTextFollowsHref call and no text replacement; the follow logic exists only in the caret branch at editor.ts:3634-3661. The same asymmetry is duplicated in packages/docs/src/view/text-box-editor.ts:1187-1193 vs 1205-1232. I searched for an upstream counterexample that would route a whole-link selection into the caret branch and found none: docs-link-popover.tsx handleApply (146-160) only bails when editingExistingLink && !getLinkAtCursor(), otherwise calls insertLink unchanged; docs-view.tsx:462-467 onLinkRequest only reads getLinkAtCursor for the prefill; text-editor.ts:1232-1237 (⌘K) and requestLink (editor.ts:3765) do not collapse the selection; toolbar/context-menu just call requestLink. expandRangeForLinks (link-run.ts:133-159) snaps a partial drag to run.start..run.end and only exempts collapsed/tableCellRange ranges, so whole-link selection is the normal drag result, making the untouched selection branch the reachable path. The task plan (docs/tasks/active/20260907-docs-link-text-and-snap-todo.md:18-27) scopes Part A to the caret branch only. Cost is user-visible (new href with stale old-URL display text — the reported symptom), so it is a spec-conformance gap rather than internal tidiness.

verdict.reason: The absence is real: expandRangeForLinks is reached only through TextEditor.setSnappedRange (text-editor.ts:2368), whose only callers are the in-cell shift+click (2016), body shift+click (2067) and updateDragSelection (2353). The double-click word-select branches write unsnapped ranges directly via Selection.setRange (in-cell 1997-2000, body 2056-2061), and Selection.setRange (selection.ts:710-713) performs no expansion. No indirect wiring exists: no dblclick/mouseup handler intercepts a double-click over a link (handleMouseDown 1868-2076, handleMouseUp 2145; link-at-mouse is read only for the read-only follow path and hover cursor), and the apply side does not compensate — insertLink consults findLinkRunAt only in its caret branch (editor.ts:3618/3690), so a partially covering range is styled partially. So double-clicking a word inside a link does leave a partial link selection, contradicting the "a link behaves as an atomic unit" invariant stated at link-run.ts:114-117. Two qualifications: (a) the triple-click half of the finding is wrong — both triple-click branches select offset 0 → block length (1988-1990, 2050-2052), which cannot partially cover a block-local link run; (b) the repo's plan explicitly limits the wiring to "drag update + shift+click extend (body and in-cell)" (todo:53-54) and separately documents the deliberate shift+arrow non-snap (todo:55-58, comment at text-editor.ts:3188), so this may be an accepted scope cut whose only residue is an unrecorded rationale (tidiness, minor). Because I could not locate issue #1038's outcome/acceptance text anywhere in the tree, I cannot confidently declare the gap non-blocking, and I found no counterexample to refute the absence — so the finding stays, with my uncertainty recorded as low confidence.
